comments.body:
This repeatedly calls `will_change()` which is quite expensive, and then does a linear search through its properties list.

One way to improve that would be to add some kind of `has_any_property(...)` method that takes a list of all the properties we care about. But that would mean checking the property and will-change in different places (plus `will-change` shouldn't have many entries usually). So I think the best thing to do would be to store `computed_values.will_change()` in a variable and use that.

I mirrored this after https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/blob/fb9286eccb3b8fd81086c22972c629548866d93c/Libraries/LibWeb/Layout/Node.cpp#L199-L204

If the `will_change()` call is expensive should I adjust this place as well?

The call to `ComputedValues::will_change()` just returns a `WillChange` struct, so it's actually pretty quick (actually we could return it by `const&` to avoid unnecessary copies, but that's a separate issue.)

The reason I made `has_property()` do a linear search is that the underlying Vector will be empty or have only one or two values the vast majority of the time. If performance is a concern here we could look at using a HashTable or bitfields instead.
So should I do something here or do we keep this as is?
Ohhh, I was looking at `ComputedProperties::will_change()` instead by mistake. 🤦‍♂️ Yeah, completely ignore what I said. 😅
